chunks: And Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Yousuf ibn Ya'qob al-Ju'fi narrated to me from his book, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Hamza narrated to us from his father and Wuhayb ibn Hafs together, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah

Regarding the saying of Allah: 'Surely Allah commands you to make over trusts to their owners and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; surely Allah admonishes you with what is excellent. Surely Allah was All-Hearing, All-Seeing.'
He said: It is the will (testament) that one of us delivers to the other.

key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: Trusts (plural of amanah), referring to duties or items to be returned

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse about 'trusts' refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific exegetical interpretation of Surah An-Nisa 4:58, identifying the 'trusts' (amanat) as the 'will' (wasiyyah) that a Muslim entrusts to another. This highlights the theological and social significance of the will not merely as a legal instrument, but as a sacred trust requiring faithful delivery, reflecting the Imam's role in clarifying divine commands for the community.
